Color.fmb -- Color selection form

Form created by: Steve Cosner, Fresno, California, USA.
 email: stevec@sfsu.edu
The latest version of this form can be downloaded from:
 http://online.sfsu.edu/sac/stevec/forms/
This version was last changed on: Nov 7, 2013

The fmb file can be compiled by Forms versions 6, 10 or 11.

This form was started as a toy to display and select colors from the color palette, and it grew into a tool to change the background color to any of the 16 million colors available in the computer environment.

There are several ways to change the background color of the screen.
1. Click on the canvas. This cycles through about 10 preselected
 colors.
2. Click on a color box in the color palette or the color matrix.
3. Change the numbers in the "Set rgb" field.
4. Using the Up and Down buttons (upper-right corner).

The Form Name field, which usually contains "COLOR" allows you to branch off to any other form you may have. Enter the form name (case-sensitive) and click Go or press F8 (Execute Query). Control-Click on the Form Name field to automatically restart this form -- used especially during development and testing.

The fields at the top center of the form allow you to enter any rgb (red, green, blue) color combination. When you leave the field, the validation trigger sets the canvas background to that color. The top field uses the 0-255 color scale. The third field down uses the 1-100 scale (same as the Forms Builder). The second field, "Canvas Actual" shows the actual color palette color used by Forms (on the web, it is often different).

The box in the upper right corner of the screen enables changing the rgb color values in the 'Set RGB' field. Clicking the Up or Down button affects one or all of the rgb color values, and sets the background color to match. Use the radio buttons or the middle +/- pushbutton to change the increment. The checkboxes indicate which colors are affected by the Up and Down buttons.

The color palette in the middle of the screen emulates the color palette in the Forms Builder. When you click on any of the color boxes, the screen's background color changes to match, and the numbers in the fields indicate the color chosen. You can use the up or down-arrow keys as well as Tab and shift-Tab to move the cursor from one box to the next.

The matrix on the lower part of the screen shows a gradient of colors. Click on the various radio buttons and pushbuttons to change the parameters of the matrix, and watch the changes. (Use the Show Matrix button the first time on the Web.)

The matrix works nicely with Client/Server forms, but in Web Forms the gradient is severely limited -- Web Forms will only display colors directly from the color palette, and the first 48 colors assigned in the matrix. After that no others are available, so the gradient matrix is a patchwork of odd colors. Changing the Odd/Even radio buttons on the web version illustrates how being off by just one unit causes big changes in the color matrix.

On the matrix, Select the 'Web' vertical and horizontal radio buttons and the 'grb' color combination to see a copy of the color palette colors. With this setup, clicking the 'B' +32 and -32 buttons shifts the matrix to duplicate each of the five 6x6 blocks in the palette.

When you select a color, the form places an 'X' on the color palette matching the color. If there is no exact match (you entered rgb numbers that are not the same as any color palette color), the form tries to find the closest match, and places an 'O' on the color box.

On the Web version, below the box in the upper right corner, there is a checkbox labeled "Set button color". Check the box, and the buttons change color as you change the canvas color. Uncheck the box and the buttons remain the last-selected color.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------*

Additional notes may be found within the form fmb file in the NOTES form-level trigger.

PROCEDURE AA (M varchar2) IS --?
/* --------------------------------------------------------------------*
Setup: To set up a form you want to test, follow these steps:
(See "Using This Procedure" below for help calling this process.)

 1. Copy this procedure into your form.

 2. Do one of either 2a or 2b:
 2a. Copy the DEBUG button from block B1 to your form, and
 make sure its two triggers (when-mouse-click and
 when-button-pressed) are also included.

 2b. ... or: Create a When-Mouse-Click trigger on any item in the
 form (remember which item you use), and place the following
 two lines of code in the trigger:

-- When-Mouse-Click trigger to operate the AA debugging procedure.
aa('CONTROL'); --? Don't forget to delete this when testing is done.

------------------------------------------
Cleanup:
After testing is completed in a form, Delete this procedure
and the button or When-Mouse-Click trigger created above.
The '--?' string is what I use to search for things to remove
when testing is completed.
------------------------------------------
Note:
Do NOT use a pushbutton with a WHEN-BUTTON-PRESSED trigger to activate
debugging, because the shift keys (Ctrl, Alt and Shift) are not
correctly recognized by Forms in the when-button-pressed trigger. You
should only use when-mouse-click. (A workaround, if the WBP trigger
MUST be used: Also create a when-mouse-down trigger with a single
null; command. This causes Forms to properly set shift key data.)
------------------------------------------

Using This Procedure
--------------------
 Procedure AA stores and displays debugging messages. To see a 
 message from anywhere in your form, simply code a command such as:
 aa('Any message here');
 If debugging has been activated (by clicking the Debug button),
 the message is stored for display when requested.
 
 The input M parameter is used to pass debugging messages and also
 to control the debug process. If the text in M is anything other
 than the control values below, it is considered a message to be
 stored and displayed.

 If the first character of the message is > or ", the message is sent
 to dbms_output rather than stored immediately in the record group.
 It then shows up within the DBMS_Output message stream when you
 display the debugging messages. This is useful when database
 triggers or packages issue dbms_output messages, so you can see all
 messages, both from your form as well as the server-side messages
 in sequence. (Alternately to using the > or " redirection character,
 if a stored procedure/package issues dbms_output messages, you can
 issue this command immediately after calling the procedure:
 aa('DBMS_OUTPUT.QDISPLAY'); This will copy all dbms_output messages
 into the debugging messages queue.)

 Control commands: If the M parameter is set to any of the values
 below, they are used as controls to direct this process. Normally,
 you do not need to code any message calls to use these commands,
 since they are already set up in the 'Click_control' procedure
 below, which is used by a call from the B1.DEBUG button.
 If M is any of the following values, this process performs the
 described action:
 'TOGGLE' to turn on/off message storage
 'TOGGLEI' turn on message storage AND display messages to screen
 immediately as they are generated.
 'TOGGLE0' (TOGGLE and Zero) Turn off message storage
 'TOGGLE1' Turn on message storage
 'SHOW_MSGS' to display messages via zdebug form
 'CLEAR' to delete all stored messages
 'DBMS_OUTPUT.ENABLE Starts dbms_output recording. This is auto-
 matically turned on when message storage is started.

 Use DBMS_OUTPUT.QDISPLAY immediately after calling a
 stored procedure to display messages produced by that
 procedure.
 'DBMS_OUTPUT.DISABLE' Stops dbms_output recording AND clears any
 messages stored in the dbms_output buffer.
 'CONTROL' is issued from the When-Mouse-Click trigger. Controls
 actions within this process. Actions are described in the
 notes in the WMC trigger on the debug button.
 anything else: writes into rec group 'ZDEBUG' or to DBMS_Output;
*/

 RG RecordGroup := find_group('ZDEBUG');
 DBMS_OutB Boolean := False;
 Toggle_msg varchar2(100);

 Procedure msg(M1 varchar2) is begin
 -- Msgs starting with > or " are dbms_Output msgs.

 Else

 if substr(:GLOBAL.ZDEBUG_MSG_FLAG,1,1) = 'I' -- I = Immediate msg:
 and not DBMS_OutB then --Don't echo dbms_output to screen
 -- Also write message to screen in a pop-up window --
 if :GLOBAL.ZDEBUG_MSG_FLAG = 'I' then
 Message(M1);
 message(' ',no_acknowledge);

 Message(M1);

 Procedure DBMS_Out(M2 varchar2) is -- process DBMS_Output commands
 -- Cmds are ENABLE, DISABLE, DISPLAY. First char can be Q,
 -- Q=Quiet mode: Enabled/Disabled messages are suppressed
 quiet boolean := False;
 procedure QMsg(M varchar2) is begin
 if not quiet then Msg(M); end if;
 end QMsg;
 Begin
 --if nvl(:GLOBAL.ZDEBUG_MSG_FLAG,' ') = 'N' then
 -- return; -- do nothing
 --end if;
 If substr(M2,1,1)='Q' then
 quiet := True;
 End if;
 If M2 in('ENABLE','QENABLE') then
 dbms_output.enable(128000); --Starts dbms_output processing
 QMsg('---- DBMS_Output enabled ----');
 elsif M2 in('DISABLE','QDISABLE') then
 dbms_output.disable; --Stop dbms_output processing
 QMsg('---- DBMS_Output disabled. Buffer also cleared. ----');
 elsif M2 in('DISPLAY','QDISPLAY') then
 Declare
 cntr Pls_Integer := 0;
 Sts Integer;
 txt varchar2(300);
 Begin
 DBMS_OutB := True;
 Loop
 dbms_output.get_line(txt,sts);
 if sts=0 then
 if cntr = 0 then
 Msg('---- The following lines are from DBMS_Output ----');
 end if;
 cntr:= cntr+1;
 Msg(txt);
 else
 if cntr=0 then
 QMsg('---- End of DBMS_Output, no lines available.');
 else
 Msg('---- End of DBMS_Output, displayed '
 ||cntr||' lines. Buffer also cleared.');
 end if;
 exit;
 end if;
 End loop;
 DBMS_OutB := False;
 End;
 end if ;
 End DBMS_Out;
BEGIN
 -- Initialization: create global variable and record group
 Default_value('N','GLOBAL.ZDEBUG_MSG_FLAG');
 if id_null(RG) then
 RG := Create_group_from_query('ZDEBUG',
 'Select rpad(chr(32),2000) as TXT from dual',
 Global_Scope);
 end if;
 ----
 if upper(M) = 'CONTROL' then
 --- Debug button clicked --
 Click_Control;
 elsif upper(M) = 'SHOW_MSGS' then 
 --- Show Messages ---
 DBMS_Out('QDISPLAY');
 If get_group_row_count(RG) = 0
 and id_null(find_timer('ZDEBUG')) then
 Msg2(' No messages to display. '
 ||'Click again (within 5 seconds) to call zDebug form.');
 if id_null(Create_timer('ZDEBUG',5000,no_repeat)) then
 null;
 end if;
 else
 Clear_Message;
 Call_Form('ZDEBUG',No_hide);
 end if;
 ---
 elsif substr(upper(M),1,6) = 'TOGGLE' then
 --- Toggle Messages ---
 If upper(M)='TOGGLEI' then
 :GLOBAL.ZDEBUG_MSG_FLAG := 'I';
 DBMS_Out('QENABLE');
 Btn_label := 'Set Msg flag OFF';
 Toggle_msg := 'Msg_Flag set to I -- Messages output to screen';
 elsif upper(M)='TOGGLE1'
 or upper(M)='TOGGLE'
 and nvl(:GLOBAL.ZDEBUG_MSG_FLAG,' ') in('N',' ') then
 :GLOBAL.ZDEBUG_MSG_FLAG := 'Y';
 DBMS_Out('QENABLE');
 Btn_label := 'Set Msg flag OFF';
 Toggle_msg := 'Msg_Flag set to Y -- Messages can now '
 ||'be created. Msgs='|| get_group_row_count('ZDEBUG');
 else -- all other conditions:
 -- M='TOGGLE0' or M='TOGGLE' and Global in('Y','I')
 :GLOBAL.ZDEBUG_MSG_FLAG := 'N';
 DBMS_Out('QDISABLE');--stops msg recording AND clears msg buffer
 Btn_label := 'Set Msg flag ON';
 Toggle_msg := 'Msg_Flag set to N -- Messages will no longer '
 ||'be created. Msgs='|| get_group_row_count('ZDEBUG');
 end if;
 Msg2(' ' || Toggle_msg);
 -- If running inside zDebug form, change button label:
 If not id_null(find_item('B1.DEBUG_MSG_ON_OFF')) then
 set_item_property('B1.DEBUG_MSG_ON_OFF',Label,Btn_Label);
 End if;
 ---
 elsif upper(M) = 'CLEAR' then
 --- Clear Messages ---
 DBMS_Out('QDISABLE');--stops msg recording AND clears msg buffer

 DBMS_Out('QENABLE');
 end if;
 Msg2(' All ( '||get_group_row_count(RG)
 ||' ) stored messages cleared. Msg_Flag='
 ||:GLOBAL.ZDEBUG_MSG_FLAG);
 delete_group_row(RG,all_rows);
 ---
 elsif upper(substr(M,1,12)) = 'DBMS_OUTPUT.' then
 DBMS_Out(upper(substr(M,13)));
 elsif nvl(:GLOBAL.ZDEBUG_MSG_FLAG,' ') <> 'N' then
 Msg(M); -- store/display msg
 end if;
END AA;

 function get_1_255_colors(txt_i varchar2) return varchar2 is
 -------------------------
 -- converts Forms builder colors (0-100) to runtime colors (0-255).
 -- example: r50g100b75 --> r127g255b191
 -- If all three values are between 0 and 100, the conversion is
 -- completed. If any is > 100 then txt_i is assumed to already
 -- be a 0-255 color, and txt_i is returned unchanged.
 rtrn varchar2(12);
 rtrnW varchar2(12);
 rWeb varchar2(3);
 c pls_integer := 0;
 p pls_integer;
 function conv(v in varchar2) return varchar2 is
 v2 varchar2(3);
 begin
 if num(v) between 0 and 100 then
 c := c+1;
 if v in('0','25','50','75','88','100') then
 if v='0' then v2:='0'; elsif v='25' then v2:='63';
 elsif v='50' then v2:='127'; elsif v='75' then v2:='191';
 elsif v='88' then v2:='223'; else v2:='255'; end if;
 If get_application_property(user_interface) = 'WEB'
 and v2 not in('0', '255') then
 v2 := num(v2) + 1;--better match of web forms palette
 end if;
 else
 v2 := trunc(num(v)*2.55);
 end if;
 end if;
 Rweb := v;
 if num(v) between 1 and 254
 and get_application_property(user_interface) = 'WEB'
 and num(v) mod 2 = 1 then
 Rweb := num(v) + 1;
 end if; 
 return v2;
 end conv;
 begin
 begin
 p := instr(txt_i,'r')+1;
 rtrn := 'r'||conv(substr(txt_i,p,instr(txt_i,'g')-p));
 rtrnW:= 'r'||rWeb;
 p := instr(txt_i,'g')+1;

 rtrnW:= rtrnW||'g'||rWeb;
 rtrn := rtrn ||'b'||conv(substr(txt_i,instr(txt_i,'b')+1 ));
 rtrnW:= rtrnW||'b'||rWeb;
 exception when others then c:=0;
 end;
 if c <> 3 then -- all values were not 1 to 100; ex: some > 100
 rtrn := txt_i;

Procedure P08_Calc_Interval(H_V varchar2,show_matrix boolean) is
-- Recalculate vertical or horizontal scale of the matrix.
-- Sets the values displayed in the 5 vertical or 5 horizontal
-- scale items.
-- Called from WNFI and WRC triggers;
--
 c_interval pls_integer;
 v1 pls_integer;
 v3 pls_integer;
 v5 pls_integer;
 v7 pls_integer;
 v9 pls_integer;
Begin
 If H_V = 'V' then
 v1 := :B4.v1;
 c_interval := :B4.interval_v;
 Else
 v1 := :B4.h1;
 c_interval := :B4.interval_h;
 End if;

 If c_interval = 99 then -- Web range
 v1 := 0;
 v3 := 128;
 v5 := 224;
 v7 := 256;
 v9 := null;
 Else
 v1 := greatest(0, v1);
 v1 := v1 + v1 mod 2; --if v1 is an odd number then add 1.
 -- So all interval values will be even numbers.
 v9 := v1 + 8 * c_interval;
 if v9 > 256 then
 v9 := 256;
 v1 := greatest(0, v9 - 8 * c_interval);
 end if;
 v3 := v1 + 2 * c_interval;
 v5 := v1 + 4 * c_interval;
 v7 := v1 + 6 * c_interval;
 End if;
 If :B4.Odd_Even_Radgrp = 'O' then -- uppercase O, not zero
 -- convert to odd numbers
 v1 := greatest(0, v1 - 1);
 v3 := v3 - 1;
 v5 := v5 - 1;
 v7 := v7 - 1;
 v9 := v9 - 1;
 Else
 v7 := least(255, v7);
 v9 := least(255, v9);
 End if;
 If H_V = 'V' then
 :B4.v1:=v1; :B4.v3:=v3; :B4.v5:=v5; :B4.v7:=v7; :B4.v9:=v9;
 Else
 :B4.h1:=v1; :B4.h3:=v3; :B4.h5:=v5; :B4.h7:=v7; :B4.h9:=v9;
 End if;
 --If mode1 in ('WRC') then
 If show_matrix then
 P01_Show_Matrix;
 End if;
End P08_Calc_Interval;

PROCEDURE P15_Set_X_O_checkmarks
 ( blk_list varchar2,
 NewColor varchar2,
 Mode1 varchar2)

-- Find matching color box in each block of color boxes.
-- Blk_list specifies which blocks to check, B2, B3 and B5.
-- Step through all items in each block and find the item
-- with the color most closely matching the canvas background color.
-- Sets X_O_ChkMark to X if a perfect match (r,g,b values off by 4 or
-- less. Sets X_O_ChkMark to O if value off by no more than
-- 50 in B2, 500 in B3, and 100 in B5.
-- Mode1 indicates caller of this process. Most come from P04.
is
 Match_Itm varchar2(50);
 Match_Itm2 varchar2(50);
 X_O_ChkMark varchar2(1);
 cnv_bgd varchar2(20);
 color_name varchar2(50);
 Itm1 Varchar2(50);
 Itm1_color Varchar2(20);
 match pls_integer := 1000;
 match1 pls_integer;
 r pls_integer;
 r1 pls_integer;
 g pls_integer;
 g1 pls_integer;
 b pls_integer;
 b1 pls_integer;
 P14_sts boolean;
 Timer_1 timer;
 --
 Procedure Find_Color_in_block(blk varchar2) is begin
 -----------------------------
 If Mode1 = 'WNII'
 and :system.trigger_block = blk then
 match := 0;
 Match_Itm := :System.trigger_item;
 Else
 match := 1000;
 Match_itm := Null;
 Itm1 := get_block_property(blk,first_item);
 Loop
 Itm1 := blk ||'.'|| Itm1;
 -- if blk=B5, need to use hint_text
 If blk<>'B5' then
 Itm1_color := get_item_property(Itm1,background_color);
 Else

 End if;
 If Itm1_color = cnv_bgd then
 match := 0;
 Match_itm := Itm1;
 else
 P14_parse_rgb(Itm1_color,P14_sts,r,g,b);
 if P14_sts then
 match1 := abs(r-r1)+abs(g-g1)+abs(b-b1);
 if match > match1 then
 match := match1;
 Match_itm := Itm1;
 end if;
 end if;
 end if;
 exit when match = 0;
 Itm1 := get_item_property(Itm1,nextitem);
 Exit when Itm1 is null;
 End loop;
 End if;
 If match > 4 then
 X_O_ChkMark := 'O';
 Else
 X_O_ChkMark := 'X';
 If Match_Itm2 is null then
 Match_Itm2 := Match_itm;
 End if;
 End if;
 -- if exact match and color box has a hint (= name of color)
 -- display that color in the field on the screen.
 If X_O_ChkMark = 'X'
 and :B1.color_name is null
 and Blk <> 'B5' then
 Color_name
 := ltrim(rtrim(get_item_property(Match_Itm,hint_text)));
 If color_name is not null then
 :B1.color_name := color_name;
 P11_Check_color(NewColor,Color_name);
 End if;
 End if;

 Find_Color_in_block(blk);

aa('P15 set P0.WNII_NOGO := True');

 end Chk_one_blk;

-- When window resized form-level trigger
Declare
 Win varchar2(20) := :System.event_window;
 W_Id window := Find_window(Win);
 Hlp item;
 N_itm pls_integer;
 N_win pls_integer;
 N_calc pls_integer;
Begin
 If Win = 'HELP' then
 -- Adjust height and width of help screen field, B1.Help so it
 -- always fills the window, no matter what the window dimensions.
 Hlp := Find_item('B1.HELP');
 -- Adjust height of B1.Help --
 N_itm := Get_item_property (Hlp, height);
 N_win := Get_window_property(W_Id,height);
 N_calc := greatest(17, N_win - 77);
 If N_calc <> N_itm then
 Set_item_property(Hlp,height,N_calc);
 End if;
 -- Adjust width of B1.Help --
 N_itm := Get_item_property (Hlp, width);
 N_win := Get_window_property(W_Id,width);
 N_calc := greatest(82, N_win - 20);
 If N_calc <> N_itm then
 If N_calc < 290 then
 if to_number(get_item_property('B1.CANCEL_HELP',x_pos)) > 4 then
 Set_item_property('B1.CANCEL_HELP',x_pos,4);
 end if;
 Elsif to_number(get_item_property('B1.CANCEL_HELP',x_pos))<209 then
 Set_item_property('B1.CANCEL_HELP',x_pos,209);
 End if;
 Set_item_property(Hlp,width,N_calc);
 End if;
 
 ElsIf Get_window_property('HELP',Visible) = 'FALSE' then
 Declare
 W0 Window := Find_Window('WINDOW0');
 Begin
 If Get_Window_Property(W0,Window_State)<>'MAXIMIZE' then
 Set_Window_Property(W0,Window_State,Maximize);
 End if;
 End;
 Elsif Get_Application_Property(User_Interface) <> 'WEB' then
 Set_Window_Property(Forms_MDI_Window,Title,:SYSTEM.CURRENT_FORM);
 End if;
End;
